evidence: The study's inputs other than the technology paths, each with its value and basis: a lookup or design it was read from, or the study's own value with its range where no source has been found. Five entries carry design choices that are still open (choices 1 to 5 of the README); each is set to the option recommended on 16 November until it is settled, and the others can be run as cases.
reading_rule: An entry is a value with its basis, or a group of such entries. Money is in constant dollars of 2041 unless the key names another year. Rates of work are at 2041 and change with the roadmap's output per job.

USD2026_to_USD2041.basis: the staged studies' normalization at 3% a year (provisioning/vacuum_industry)

pay_counted.basis: choice 1, open: the account with Earth counts the share of residents' pay spent on Earth; 'all' counts the whole payroll as the coupled study did

wage_USD2041_year.basis: the coupled study's worker's year in 2041 (its programme.json, opportunity_USD2041_worker_year), without a source; about 1.5 times a high-income average wage, as Australian mining pays 1.55 times the average (I12); it follows the world's income per person after 2041, as OECD median wages followed productivity within 5-8% over 1995-2013 (I20)

equipment_USD2026_kg.basis: I01 (2023 export values): rock-moving and crushing machinery 6-17 USD/kg; machine tools, bearings, motors and robots 9-52; power electronics and batteries 41-76; spacecraft 4,700-69,000. The staged model's 500 is carried for equipment made in series to work on the Moon, between the industrial and the spacecraft anchors; it follows the roadmap's price multiple.

supplies_USD2026_kg.basis: the staged model's special imports, without a source

financing.basis: choice 5, open: the coupled study's arrangements in U are left for a later layer

computing_hardware_USD2026_kg.basis: I01: computers and chip-making machines 190-260 USD/kg, integrated circuits about 1,800 (2023 export values); 500 for servers built to work on the Moon, the study's own

dollars_held_share_of_output.basis: the dollars a zone without money of its own holds for its residents and firms to pay one another, as a share of its output, which it must earn from Earth as its output grows: replacing a domestic currency costs a stock of 8% of output on 1970s data and 4-5% in the late 1990s, and the seigniorage given up is 0.1-0.3% of output a year at low inflation (JEC00); dollarized banks hold liquidity of 23% of deposits and more (El Salvador, Panama; Swiston11). The middle of 4-8%, with the ends as the range (lookup of 17 November 2026, research drive vacuum-economy/research/u_premia_money_trade/values.md)

births_per_resident_year.basis: choice 2, open: about the world's natural increase today; no human birth in low gravity has been observed

launched_kg_per_passenger.basis: scenarios.json visits: 270 kg a passenger in one published estimate of a seat to orbit (P23)

cabin_kg_per_passenger.basis: scenarios.json visits, constructed: cabin, air, water and stores carried for each passenger between low Earth orbit and the Moon

founding_crew.basis: the study's own: the people who build the opening settlements in years 0 to 7 and become its first residents

share_who_work.basis: I19, I20: the employed share of the whole population of high-income countries 45% (1991) to 49% (2024), 55% in Japan; a settlement of working-age arrivals carries the upper value

service_jobs_per_resident.basis: the study's own: about a third of the workforce serving the residents (health, schools, administration, shops, homes) at 2041

teleoperation.basis: I18: a laboratory excavator task took 174% of its undelayed time with the 3 s delay of operators on Earth (success fell from 91% to 45%); I03, I05: the factory concepts are run from Earth at first. Work the residents cannot staff in the industry is done from Earth, a job-year costing an Earth wage (the lunar wage over the 1.55 premium of remote mining, I12) times 1.74, paid to Earth.

landscape_water_kg_day.basis: design: the inherited landscape and other makeup allowance, kept whatever the recovery

regional_hall_shielding_t_per_m2_floor.basis: the study's extension of the designs: three metres of regolith at 1,600 kg/m3 over 1.22 m2 of hall envelope a square metre of floor (the city halls' envelope over their floor) for regional halls built outside a cave

caves_for_cities.basis: choice 3: no city-sized cave is confirmed; the founding four are conditional (lava_tube_cities)

crater_sites.basis: habitation/crater_gardens/buildout.json: 0.1% of the 8,886,558 catalogued craters 200-1,000 m across

eventual_crater_sites.basis: habitation/crater_gardens/buildout.json: 2.5% of the 8,886,558 catalogued craters 200-1,000 m across, rounded down, the eventual set to which the initial quota belongs. Growth past the initial quota builds towns of the case's size on the eventual set's further sites (agreed 16 November 2026); no crater towns are planned beyond it, the conservation framework's sixth principle leaving the rest of the land unassigned

town_residents.basis: design (the first hundred towns' cases): towns after the founding system follow the 750-resident case, 291 m craters, since the plan's 6.47 million on the 8,886 sites of the initial quota is about 730 a site; the founding system's towns keep their 500

town_sites_within_km_of_a_polar_ridge.basis: computed from the crater count's 902,291 candidate sites (research drive, crater-settlements/candidates.csv.gz, sha256 ede1a1fbbcde20dadaf90a1ff08748fd252fe12f0690598c8583cdb910543ad2): distance along the surface from latitude 89 degrees, at 30.32 km a degree

city_km_from_a_polar_ridge.basis: the four lava-tube search regions lie between 8 and 36 degrees north (lava_tube_cities README); the nearest, at 36 degrees, is 1,600 km from latitude 89

renewal_life_years.basis: design (lava_tube_cities maintenance lives): ordinary durable stock and farm structure 80 years; supports 100 and reinforcement 50, carried as 60 for metal; liners 25 and reinforcement 50, carried as 35 for pressure components; production equipment 20, lengthened by the roadmap's life multiple. Handling, shielding and the first air and water are not renewed.

local_goods_mineral_share.basis: design: of 12,500 t of new material a year for everyday goods, 10,000 t local mineral feed and 2,500 t imported carbon feed (counted with the supplies)

industry.basis: Rates of work and the plant masses of the bulk lines are the study's own; the factory line's output per kilogram follows I03; energies are the designs' where stated.

handling.kWh_basis: design: the first hundred towns' handling energy over the regolith handled

bulk.kWh_basis: design: the first hundred towns' bulk energy over the bulk products

manufactured.plant_basis: I03: factories of 6-100 t make 0.5-1 kg a year per kilogram of factory

water.plant_basis: the study's own: mining and heating plant at the sources handling about 700 kg of 7% rock a year per kilogram of plant (bulk excavators move thousands of times their mass a year)

propellant.kWh_basis: the study's own: electrolysis and liquefaction of water at the depot
propellant.plant_basis: the study's own: electrolysers and liquefiers at the depot

local_manufacture_ramp_years.basis: L1: the imported share of equipment falls to its floor over 12 to 30 years from the start of local production

industry_power_firm_factor.basis: the study's own margin on the industry's mean load

industry.jobs_basis: the study's own at 2041: 10,000 t a job-year handled, 500 t of bulk products, 50 t of metal, 5 t of manufactured goods (US machinery makers produce about 18 t a worker-year, the study's estimate), 1,000 t of water at the sources, 2,000 t of propellant

plant_margin.basis: the study's own: each line's plant is sized a quarter above the work asked of it from outside, the margin on which the industry builds its own plant and meets years of uneven work

night_hours.basis: E2: the lunar night away from the poles

storage_local_share.basis: the study's own: tanks and structure made on the Moon, stacks and controls bought

beam_constellation_factor.basis: design: ten stations with two carrying the load (the compact model's reading of the founding design)

upkeep_share_year.basis: the study's own: upkeep of power plant each year, as a share of its capital

launch_payload_kg.basis: E4: a fully reusable heavy launcher's payload

launches_per_pad_year.basis: T5: the largest authorised rate found for a heavy-lift complex

moon_to_depot_m_s.basis: T1: lunar surface to low lunar orbit about 1.9 km/s and on to the depot near the Earth-Moon L1 point; the study's rounding

chemical_isp_s.basis: hydrogen and oxygen from water (the founding tug)

tug_max_dry_kg_per_kg_year.basis: the study's own practical limit: a tug design that would weigh more than five times the water it delivers in a year is not flown, and a leg that no tug flies within it lies beyond reach. Near the end of a tug's reach its mass per kilogram delivered grows without bound (nuclear-electric tugs need 11 to 26 kg a kilogram a year at 6.5 to 7 km/s, electric ones under 1 kg), and the choice by cost, which prices a tug at the settlement's own manufacturing, would otherwise build fleets far faster than any factory can grow and buy the rest from Earth

tug_round_trip_years.basis: the founding tug's three-year round trip

electric_isp_s.basis: L5: thrusters on water, development target 2,000 s

electric_powered_years.basis: the coupled study's electric tug: one powered year in a three-year cycle

electric_leg_multiple.basis: the coupled study's electric tug: the impulsive leg times 1.6 for slow thrust

reach_percentile.basis: the source survey's contained water by velocity change (resources/source_access/results/reach.json.gz)

water_set_aside_share.decided: 16 November 2026: the set-asides are on by default in every case; the whole pool is a comparison
water_set_aside_share.basis: the share of each body's contained water left unmined, on by default. 0.9 is the project's only stated set-aside, the world economy study's synthetic reservation shares (research/studies/world_economy/amenities_inputs.json, mining: 40% for future use, 30% protected, 20% withheld for uncertainty, from the register's rule of 31 October 2026 not to strip what is needed later), applied evenly to the near-Earth bodies; 0 counts the survey's whole conditional pool, as a comparison. The conservation framework draws water from ordinary icy bodies only, and every near-Earth body in the survey is one; no approved extraction fraction exists

electric_drive_USD2026_W.basis: the coupled study's electric tug: drives at 5 USD2026 a watt

electric_drive_life_years.basis: the coupled study's electric tug: worn out after about ten years in service

depot_propellant_per_kg_landed_from_Eart.basis: the study's own: the descent from the depot and the lander's return on depot propellant, from year 20 when the coupled study moved the Earth leg's propellant to the depot; before, the Earth leg carries its own

asteroid_water_grade.basis: E5: water in carbonaceous asteroids 5%, 7% and 13%; the feed mined is the contained water drawn over the grade

visitor_cap_share.basis: the compact model's bound: the share of the world's people who could visit in a year, the study's own

computing_hardware_kg_W.basis: the study's own: about 15 kg of servers, racks and cooling a kilowatt

computing_overhead.basis: the study's own: cooling and distribution over the servers' power

depot_sales_cap_multiple.basis: the study's own bound, like the bound on visits: propellant and material sold at the depot at most this many times the scenario's 2049 quantity grown with activity in space, saturating smoothly, since one elasticity at every price would otherwise sell without limit as costs fall

rule.basis: choice 4: the steady rule as headline (agreed 16 November 2026), with the fastest rule beside. Steady growth is solved in two stages: the highest single rate from the opening to the plan, then the highest single rate past it

test.basis: agreed 16 November 2026: growth is carried while the funders earn 3% (net present value at 3% to the horizon not negative) and, once the account with Earth is repaid, the settlement pays its own way: no ten years after the repayment are together in deficit with Earth; the settlement's own work staffed, the sources' water not exhausted and every newcomer housed within the eventual set of sites. The ten-year window is the study's reading of the agreed rule of no yearly deficit: a single year's reinvestment, such as a change of power supply that the factories cannot yet make in full and buy in part from Earth, would otherwise stop all growth, while a lasting deficit still fails. A test on the present value alone admits deficits of tens of trillions a year late in the horizon, since two centuries of discounting shrink them

past_plan.basis: agreed 16 November 2026: growth continues past the planned 6.47 million wherever resources allow, the plan being a milestone each case reports. The programme's ramps carry on past 2241 at their final rates (constant growth 3.31% a year, front-loaded 1.97%) until the sites are full; 'hold' keeps the version of 12c50265, residents held at the plan

horizon_year.basis: agreed 16 November 2026: the projection runs to 2341, with technology held at its 2241 values (period_technology.json holds every path after its last year) and Earth's demand on its scenario's growth

exhaustion_horizon_year.basis: the study's own: the rough projection of when the sites and the sources' water run out continues each path's growth until a resource runs out or to 3541, technology still held at 2241

opening_funding_limit.basis: the coupled study's rule for residents as a result: the opening funding may be no larger than the constant-growth ramp's

u.basis: U, the money of the zone beyond Earth, beside the account with Earth, as designed on 16 November 2026 and given an exchange rate on 17 November 2026: one U for the accounts (Terluna's later work splits it into several zones); the share of trade settled in U; Earth's customers' and sellers' working balances; Earth's investors holding U assets at a real yield; the share of their income spent in the zone, whose goods the economy charges to the lines' costs; any effect of paying in U on Earth's purchases; the funders' returns paid partly in U; U's rate in dollars, at par until the account with Earth is repaid and floating after it down to a floor; a partial reserve kept at its target by the funders during the build and rebuilt from surpluses after, held as a basket of Earth's currencies and metals; and the inflation U allows. Amounts in dollars are constant dollars of 2041 of purchasing power; amounts in U are U of constant purchasing power in the zone, each worth the year's rate in dollars. The holders' behaviour is checked against the lookup of 16 November 2026 (research drive, vacuum-economy/research/u_monetary_policy/values.md, with its source keys); the share of income spent in the zone and Earth's safe real rate remain the study's own

policy.basis: the account with Earth in dollars alone, as before, until the default is set; the U policies run as cases

conservative.basis: the policy of 12-13 November 2026: inflation in U kept low, with room for mild expansion, and a partial reserve; trade settled in U from 25% to 85% over the ten years after the opening, the earlier price-pressure study's reference transition (research/studies/monetary_system/pressure.md); no yield offered to Earth's investors; the reserve's target half of Earth's holdings and a year of payments to Earth, which leaves six months of payments between the target and the tests' minimum for the reserve to absorb before U moves; a fifth of the reserve in gold and platinum-group metals, within the 16-27% of the world's official reserves gold makes at end-2023 and end-2025 prices (ECB26) and above the 0-7% most small open economies hold (WGC26; Ecuador 37.5%), taken first from the zone's own refining; the metals earn nothing, Jastram's long-run real return on gold (EH13), against 1.3% a year since 1900 (DMS26); each instrument is held by its own group (17 November 2026): Earth's investors hold bonds of ten years, a tenth falling due each year; the holders for use stake (u.holders); stakes lock for two years; the funders keep their U liquid, with their staking a case

liberal.basis: a more liberal policy at the edge of the five tests: bonds or staking at a real yield of 2% a year, held within the zone's growth over the twenty years before once that is known, inflation at the decade bound of 3%, the reserve's target a quarter of Earth's holdings and six months of payments, at the tests' minimum, so that U's rate moves as soon as the account leaves the reserve short; a quarter of the funders' returns paid in U, with the policy search trying none to half, and trade settled in U up to 95%; a fifth of the reserve in gold and platinum-group metals, within the 16-27% of the world's official reserves gold makes at end-2023 and end-2025 prices (ECB26) and above the 0-7% most small open economies hold (WGC26; Ecuador 37.5%), taken first from the zone's own refining; the metals earn nothing, Jastram's long-run real return on gold (EH13), against 1.3% a year since 1900 (DMS26); each instrument is held by its own group (17 November 2026): Earth's investors hold bonds of ten years, a tenth falling due each year; the holders for use stake (u.holders); stakes lock for two years; the funders keep their U liquid, with their staking a case

floor.basis: the lowest rate, in dollars a U at par, to which U may fall once the account with Earth is repaid: what the residents' pay buys of Earth's goods may fall by at most this much against par. A setting chosen on 17 November 2026, run at par, 75% and 50%; 75% is the default of the cases that do not name one

metal_haircut.basis: the share of the metals' value the run test leaves out, as the transition plan's illustrative 10% haircut on reserve value (research/studies/monetary_system/trade_transition.md); the metals earn nothing and hold their value in constant dollars

backstop_after_repayment.basis: what stands behind the reserve once the account with Earth is repaid, when U at its floor still leaves the reserve below its minimum: the funders' credit line lends it the rest and their flows carry the loan, judged by the same decade test as the dollar account, in which the funders cover a year's deficit so long as no ten years together are in deficit; with none, the reserve falls short and fails its test. Credit line by default since 17 November 2026, none as the stricter case

earth_safe_real_rate.basis: provisional: the real return Earth's investors have without the zone, about the long-run real yield on reserve-currency government debt; the reserve earns it

investment_threshold_spread.basis: the real return above Earth's safe rate below which Earth's investors hold no U assets: the premium a new or small currency pays. Survey-based currency premia over 1996-2018 average 4.2 points a year for 22 emerging markets (median 3.5, quartiles 0.6 and 7.0) and 0.9 for 12 advanced economies (KV26); the smallest OECD currencies earned 5.8% a year against 2.0 for the largest (Hassan12); New Zealand's indexed bonds yielded 1 to 1.5 points over the United States' (Reddell15, Reddell18); the dollar's own premium is 0.1-0.2 points (DIS17). Taken at the emerging markets' median, 3.5 points, with the small advanced economies' 1 point and the upper quartile's 7 as the range (lookup of 17 November 2026, research drive vacuum-economy/research/u_premia_money_trade/values.md); it was a provisional 0.5 point before

investment_spread_scale.basis: the further spread over which their holdings rise toward the ceiling, by 1 - exp(-excess / scale); with the adjustment below, a point of spread draws about 3-5% of output in the first year, against net portfolio inflows of 0.34-0.58% of output a quarter per point of policy-rate differential in 12 emerging markets after 2008 (AZ14); one study finds yield differentials insignificant for local-currency bond inflows beside the dollar's moves (GPS24)

investment_ceiling_share_of_output.basis: the most Earth's investors would hold, as a share of the zone's yearly output: foreign holdings of reserve-currency government debt are about 30% of output (US 31% of debt held by the public, CRS26; Japan 12.8% of its bonds and bills, MOF26; UK 33.4% of gilts, DMO25), and non-residents held a mean 22% of 14 emerging markets' local-currency government debt in 2012-2024, 1 to 58% (GFSR25ch3), some 7 to 9% of output (lookup of 16 November 2026, research drive vacuum-economy/research/u_monetary_policy/values.md)

adjustment_per_year.basis: provisional: the share of the gap between what Earth's investors hold and want that they close in a year, buying U with dollars or converting it back

share_of_income_spent_in_zone.basis: the study's own: the share of the yield Earth's holders earn, and of the funders' U, that they spend on the zone's goods and services, paid in U and so costing the zone its own work, not dollars; no source records portfolio holders' spending in the issuer, and the nearest measure, the income direct investors keep in the host, is about a third (40% in developing hosts, WIR13)

trade_effect_of_full_settlement.basis: the change in Earth's purchases from the zone when all its trade is settled in U, scaled by the share settled; none by default (17 November 2026). The evidence on shared monies measures partners who use one money, 30-90% more trade in a meta-analysis of 34 studies (RS05) and for the euro from not significant (Hav10, LWYZ19) to 40-50% (GR16blog); moving the zone from the dollar to U puts an exchange between it and Earth, and in Glick and Rose's records of 1948-1997 trade roughly halved when a shared currency ended (GR16blog). A liquidity system that makes the market for U keeps the cost of converting small, so the default is no effect, with a 10% fall as the case of a thin market or a widely swinging U; the gain a shared money brings belongs to trade within the zone; the lookup of 17 November 2026 (vacuum-economy/research/u_premia_money_trade/values.md) puts leaving a currency union at 0 / -26 / -50% of bilateral trade (GR16, GR16EL, HMR10, GR02), much of it the decay of colonial ties after independence (65% over 40 years, HMR10), with no step change in Ireland's trade with Britain after 1979; invoicing in the exporter's own currency changes how prices and quantities answer exchange-rate moves, not the level of exports (AIK22); and exchange-rate volatility has little or no effect on trade (Clark04, BS15)

working_balance_days.basis: the earlier price-pressure study's customer holdings: Earth's customers and sellers keep seven days of the trade settled in U as working balances, without interest

holders_for_use_months.basis: the study's own: the months of their spending in the zone on its culture and visits that people on Earth keep in U, above the week of trade Earth's customers and sellers hold as working balances; no source measures how much of a currency its foreign consumers hold for later spending, so three months with one and six as the range

holders_for_use_staking_share.basis: the share of their U the holders for use stake where the policy pays a yield, locked for the staking term: about the 28-34% of ether staked at its 2.6% reward (Block24, Block26), below the median 44% of 66 proof-of-stake tokens at a median 10% reward (CHT25); the reward is spent in the zone

tests.basis: the five tests of a safe and healthy policy agreed on 16 November 2026, to be rechecked against the lookup: inflation in U at most 3% a year over any decade and never above 5% in a year; reserves of at least 20% of the U held on Earth and six months of dollar payments to Earth; a run withdrawing a quarter of Earth's holdings within a year met from the reserve; the real yield paid no higher than the zone's growth over the twenty years before; Earth's holdings no larger than the zone's yearly output. The zone's output is its residents' pay, the workforce at the wage, with what the zone keeps of its sales to Earth

build_years.basis: the study's own: the opening settlements are built in years 3 to 7 by the seed industry delivered in years 0 to 4
